clinician.final_diagnosis: c-ANCA positive IBD with prominent extraintestinal manifestations preceding GI complaints
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old man developed sequential right-sided extraintestinal inflammatory manifestations over 7 months: anterior uveitis (7 months prior), auricular chondritis (5 months later), and right wrist inflammatory arthritis initially misdiagnosed as cellulitis (2 months later). He subsequently presented with fever and diarrhea suspected to be viral gastroenteritis. Admission workup revealed marked systemic inflammation (CRP 11.1 mg/dL, ESR 124 mm/h, leukocytosis), iron deficiency anemia, and positive fecal lactoferrin. Comprehensive infectious workup was negative. c-ANCA was positive at 1:40 titer with elevated PR3 (102.6 units). Colonoscopic biopsies revealed cryptitis, crypt abscesses, and basal plasmacytosis without granulomas or vasculitis, consistent with IBD. Although chest radiograph showed a patchy infiltrate and microscopic hematuria was present, there was no renal dysfunction or proteinuria to suggest GPA. Treatment with azathioprine and infliximab resulted in fistula healing and sustained clinical remission for 1.5 years without further GI or extraintestinal manifestations, confirming the diagnosis of c-ANCA positive IBD.

final.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old man developed sequential right-sided extraintestinal inflammatory manifestations over 7 months: anterior uveitis (7 months prior), auricular chondritis (5 months later), and right wrist inflammatory arthritis initially misdiagnosed as cellulitis (2 months later). He subsequently presented with fever and diarrhea suspected to be viral gastroenteritis. Admission workup revealed marked systemic inflammation (CRP 11.1 mg/dL, ESR 124 mm/h, leukocytosis), iron deficiency anemia, and positive fecal lactoferrin. Comprehensive infectious workup was negative. c-ANCA was positive at 1:40 titer with elevated PR3 (102.6 units). Colonoscopic biopsies revealed cryptitis, crypt abscesses, and basal plasmacytosis without granulomas or vasculitis, consistent with IBD. Although chest radiograph showed a patchy infiltrate and microscopic hematuria was present, there was no renal dysfunction or proteinuria to suggest GPA. Treatment with azathioprine and infliximab resulted in fistula healing and sustained clinical remission for 1.5 years without further GI or extraintestinal manifestations, confirming the diagnosis of c-ANCA positive IBD.
